questions.q:
In a parallel plate capacitor set up, the plate area of capacitor is $2{m}^{2}$ and the plates are separated by $1m$. If the space between the plates are filled with a dielectric material of thickness $0 . 5m$ and are $2{m}^{2}$ (see figure) the capacitance of the set-up will be ${ε}_{0}$ ________.

(Dielectric constant of the material $= 3 . 2$)

(Round off to the Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
The given system can be considered as a series combination of two capacitors. The equivalent capacitance can be given as,

$\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{C}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{C}_{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{2}}{K{ε}_{0}A} + \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{2}}{{ε}_{0}A}$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{\dfrac{d}{2K} + \dfrac{d}{2}} = \dfrac{2{ε}_{0}A}{\dfrac{d}{K} + d}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times 2{ε}_{0}}{\dfrac{1}{3 . 2} + 1} = \dfrac{4 \times 3 . 2}{4 . 2}{ε}_{0}$

$= 3 . 04{ε}_{0}$

questions.q: A telegraph line of length $100km$ has a capacity of $0 . 01\muF{km}^{- 1}$ and it carries an alternating current at $0 . 5$ kilo cycle per second. If minimum impedance is required, then the value of the inductance that needs to be introduced in series is _____ $mH$. (If $\pi = \sqrt{10}$)
questions.solution:
The frequency given is $0 . 5$ kilo cycle per second $⇒ f = 500Hz ⇒ \omega = 2\pif = 1000\pirad{s}^{- 1}$.

Total capacitance of the wire is $C = 0 . 01 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100F$.

Impedance is minimum at resonance. Therefore, for minimum impedance

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

$⇒ \omegaL = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} ⇒ L = \dfrac{1}{{\omega}^{2}C} = \dfrac{1}{{1000}^{2} \times {\pi}^{2} \times 0 . 01 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100} = {10}^{- 1}H = 100mH$

questions.q: The equivalent capacitance between points $A$ and $B$ in below shown figure will be _____ $\muF$.
questions.solution:
Point $3$ and $4$ are at same potential, hence we can replace the capacitor with a wire.


Capacitors between points $A$ and $3$ are in parallel combination as shown above and their combined capacitance value will be $3C$.

This $3C$ capacitance is in series with $C$.
The equivalent capacitance of the system between points A and B is,
${C}_{AB} = \dfrac{3C \times C}{3C + C} = \dfrac{3C}{4}$
$⇒ {C}_{AB} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 8\mu F = 6\mu F$

questions.q: A composite parallel plate capacitor is made up of two different dielectric materials with different thickness (${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$) as shown in figure. The two different dielectric material are separated by a conducting foil $F$. The voltage of the conducting foil is _____ $V$.
questions.solution:
Capacitance of each capacitor

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{A3{ε}_{0}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 6A{ϵ}_{0}$ and ${C}_{2} = \dfrac{A4{ϵ}_{0}}{1} = 4A{ε}_{0}$

Here, $A$ is area of plate.

Equivalent capacitance is

${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}} = \dfrac{6A{ε}_{0} \times 4A{ε}_{0}}{6A{ε}_{0} + 4A{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{24}{10}A{ϵ}_{0}$

Now, net charge stored is ${q}_{net} = {C}_{eq}\left(\Delta V\right) = \dfrac{24}{10}A{ε}_{0}\left(100\right) = 240A{ε}_{0}$

Potential drop across ${C}_{2}$ is $\Delta{V}_{2} = \dfrac{240A{ε}_{0}}{4A{ε}_{0}} = 60V$

Thus, voltage of the conducting foil is ${V}_{foil} = 60V$

questions.q: In the circuit shown, the energy stored in the capacitor is $n\mu J$. The value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution:
The capacitor works as an open circuit in the given configuration.

The potential difference between the two plates of the capacitor will be the difference across the resistors having resistances $3Ω$ and $4Ω$.

Hence, the potential difference $\left(∆ V\right)$ across the capacitor can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\DeltaV & = & \left(\dfrac{4}{6} \times 12 - \dfrac{3}{12} \times 12\right)V \\ & = & 5V\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the energy stored in the capacitor is given by

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}C ( ∆ V{)}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required energy stored.

$\begin{cases}U & = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6\mu F \times {\left(5V\right)}^{2} \\ & = & 75\mu J\end{cases}$

questions.q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an ac source of $220V, 50Hz$. The circuit contain a resistance $R = 100Ω$ and an inductor of inductive reactance ${X}_{L} = 79 . 6Ω$. The capacitance of the capacitor needed to maximize the average rate at which energy is supplied will be ______ $\mu F$.
questions.solution:
The average rate at which energy supplied i.e. power delivered is maximum in case of the resonance, therefore

${X}_{C} = {X}_{L}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = 79 . 6Ω$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{1}{\omega \times 79 . 6} = \dfrac{1}{2\pif \times 79 . 6} = \dfrac{1}{100\pi \times 79 . 6} = 40\mu F$

Hence, $C = 40\mu F$.

questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment $S$ is a standard resistance. $R$ is a resistance wire. It is found that balancing length is $l = 25cm .$ If $R$ is replaced by a wire of hall length and half diameter that of $R$ of same material, then the balancing distance $l'$ (in $cm$ ) will now be ______________.
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{X}{R} = \dfrac{75}{25} = 3$
$R = \dfrac{pl}{A} = \dfrac{4pl}{\pi{d}^{2}}$
${R}^{'} = \dfrac{4p\left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right)}{\pi{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)}^{2}} = 2R$
$\pi{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)}^{2}$
then $\dfrac{X}{R'} = \left(\dfrac{100 - l}{l}\right)$
$\dfrac{100 - l}{l} = \dfrac{X}{2R} = \dfrac{3}{2}$
$l = 40.00cm$

questions.q: The total current supplied to the circuit as shown in figure by the $5V$ battery is _____ $A$.
questions.solution:

questions.q: Resistance are connected in a meter bridge circuit as shown in the figure. The balancing length ${l}_{1}$ is $40cm$. Now an unknown resistance $x$ is connected in series with $P$ and new balancing length is found to be $80cm$ measured from the same end. Then the value of $x$ will be _____ $Ω$.
questions.solution:
Applying balanced condition for meter bridge

Initially, $\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{40cm}{60cm} = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . \left(1\right)$

Finally, $\dfrac{P + x}{Q} = \dfrac{80cm}{20cm} = \dfrac{4}{1} . . . \left(2\right)$

Dividing equation $\left(2\right)$ by ($\left(1\right)$,

$\dfrac{P + x}{P} = 4 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 6$

$⇒ 1 + \dfrac{x}{P} = 6 ⇒ \dfrac{x}{P} = 5$

$∴ x = 5P = 5 \times 4 = 20Ω$

questions.q: The current density in a cylindrical wire of radius $4mm$ is $4 \times {10}^{6}A{m}^{- 2}$. The current through the outer portion of the wire between radial distances $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and $R$ is _____ $\piA$.
questions.solution:
Current density is defined as current per unit cross-section area. Therefore,

$i = JA = J \times \pi\left({R}^{2} - \dfrac{{R}^{2}}{4}\right)$

$⇒ i = 4 \times {10}^{6} \times \pi \times 16 \times {10}^{- 6} \times \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ i = 48\piA$

questions.q: A meter bridge setup is shown in the figure. It is used to determine an unknown resistance $R$ using a given resistor of $15Ω$. The galvanometer $\left(G\right)$ shows null defection when tapping key is at $43cm$ mark from end $A$. If the end correction for end $A$ is $2cm$, then the determined value of $R$ will be $Ω$.
questions.solution:
Using the conditions of a balanced wheatstone bridge and adding the end correction.

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{l + e}{\left(L + e\right) - \left(l + e\right)} ⇒ \dfrac{15}{\left(43 + 2\right)} = \dfrac{R}{\left(102 - 45\right)} ⇒ R = \dfrac{57}{45} \times 15$

$⇒ R = 19Ω$

questions.q: As per the given figure, if $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = - 1A{s}^{- 1}$, then the value of ${V}_{AB}$ at this instant will be ______ $V$.
questions.solution:
Given here, $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = - 1A{s}^{- 1}$

Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law to the circuit,

${V}_{A} - IR - L\dfrac{dI}{dt} - 12 = {V}_{B}$

$⇒ {V}_{A} - 2 \times 12 - 6 ( - 1 ) - 12 = {V}_{B}$

$⇒ {V}_{AB} = {V}_{A} - {V}_{B} = 36 - 6 = 30V$

If the resistance of the circuit is $5 Ω$, the force needed to move the rod in direction, as indicated, with a constant speed of $4m{s}^{- 1}$ will be _______${10}^{– 3}N$.

The force on the rod is given by

$F = ilB$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{Bvl}{R} \times lB$

questions.q: An insulated copper wire of $100$ turns is wrapped around a wooden cylindrical core of the cross-sectional area $24{cm}^{2}$. The two ends of the wire are connected to a resistor. The total resistance in the circuit is $12Ω$. If an externally applied uniform magnetic field in the core along its axis changes from $1 . 5T$ in one direction to $1 . 5T$ in the opposite direction, the charge flowing through a point in the circuit during the change of magnetic field will be _____ $mC$.
questions.solution:
The induced emf $\left(ε\right)$ in the turns of the coil can be written as

$\begin{cases}ε & = & - \dfrac{d\phi}{dt} \\ & = & iR . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

Simplify equation (1) to obtain the required charge through a point in the circuit.

$\begin{cases}- \dfrac{d\phi}{dt} & = & iR \\ & ⇒ & - \dfrac{1}{R}{∫}_{{\phi}_{1}}^{{\phi}_{2}}d\phi = ∫ idt \\ & ⇒ & q = \dfrac{{\phi}_{1} - {\phi}_{2}}{R} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Where, ${\phi}_{1}, {\phi}_{2}$ are the magnetic flux associated with the coil from two ends.

As, $\phi = NBA$, from equation (2), it can be written that

$q = \dfrac{NA}{R}\left({B}_{1} - {B}_{2}\right) . . . \left(3\right)$

where, $N,$$A$ are the number of turns and the cross-sectional area of the core respectively.

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required charge.

$\begin{cases}q & = & \dfrac{100 \times 24 \times {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2} \times \left(1 . 5T - \left(- 1 . 5T\right)\right)}{12Ω} \\ & = & 0 . 06C \times \dfrac{1000mC}{1C} \\ & = & 60mC\end{cases}$

questions.q: The electric field in a region is given by $\overset{\to}{E} = \left(\dfrac{3}{5}{E}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4}{5}{E}_{0}\overset{^}{j}\right)N{C}^{- 1}$. The ratio of flux of reported field through the rectangular surface of area $0 . 2{m}^{2}$ (parallel to $y - z$ plane) to that of the surface of area $0 . 3{m}^{2}$ (parallel to $x - z$ plane) is $a: b = a: 2,$ where $a = ?$ [Here $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{^}{k}$ are unit vectors along $x, y$ and $z$ -axes respectively]
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{E} = \left(\dfrac{3{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right)N{C}^{- 1}$

${A}_{1} = 0 . 2{m}^{2}$ [parallel to $y - z$ plane]

$= \overset{\to}{A}1 = 0 . 2{m}^{2}\overset{^}{i}$

${A}_{2} = 0 . 3{m}^{2}$ [parallel to $x - z$ plane]

$\overset{\to}{A}2 = 0 . 3{m}^{2}\overset{^}{j}$

Now, ${ϕ}_{a} = \left[\dfrac{3{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right] \cdot \left[0 . 2\overset{^}{i}\right] = \dfrac{3 \times 0 . 2}{5}{E}_{0}$

$\text{ and } {ϕ}_{b} = \left[\dfrac{3{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4{E}_{0}}{5}\overset{^}{j}\right] \cdot \left[0 . 3\overset{^}{j}\right] = \dfrac{4 \times 0 . 3}{5}{E}_{0}$

Now, $\dfrac{{ϕ}_{a}}{{ϕ}_{b}} = \dfrac{0 . 6}{1 . 2} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{a}{b}$

$⇒ a: b = 1: 2$

$⇒ a = 1$

questions.q:
A $1m$ long copper wire carries a current of $1A$. If the cross section of the wire is $2 . 0{mm}^{2}$ and the resistivity of copper is $1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$. The force experienced by moving electron in the wire is _____$\times {10}^{- 23}N$

(Charge of electron$= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C$ )
questions.solution:
Given here, length $l = 1m$, current $i = 1A$, area $A = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}m$ and resistivity $ρ = 1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$.

Resistance of wire is $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = \dfrac{1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 1}{2 \times {10}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}Ω$

Now, electric field in the wire is $E = ρJ$, where, $J = \dfrac{i}{A}$ is current density.

Thus, $E = \dfrac{iρ}{A} = iR = 1 \times \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}V{m}^{- 1}$

Electric force in terms of electric field is given by $F = qE$

Therefore, force experienced by moving electron is $F = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 1 . 36 \times {10}^{- 21}$$= 136 \times {10}^{- 23}N$

questions.q: An electron revolves around an infinite cylindrical wire having uniform linear charge density $2 \times {10}^{- 8}$ $C{m}^{- 1}$ in circular path under the influence of attractive electrostatic field as shown in the figure. The velocity of electron with which it is revolving is ______________ $\times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}$. Given mass of electron $= 9 \times {10}^{- 31}kg$
questions.solution:
The electric field is given by

$E = \left(\dfrac{2k\lambda}{r}\right)$

The required centripetal force is

$F = \left(\dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{r}\right)$

The force due to the field is equal to the required centripetal force,

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{2k\lambda}{r}\right)e = \dfrac{m{v}^{2}}{r}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2k\lambdae}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 9 \times {10}^{9} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{9 \times {10}^{- 31}}}$

$= \sqrt{1 . 6 \times 4 \times {10}^{13}} = 4 \times 2 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}$

$= 8 \times {10}^{6}m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A long solenoid with $1000turns{m}^{- 1}$ has a core material with relative permeability $500$ and volume ${10}^{3}{cm}^{3} .$ If the core material is replaced by another material having relative permeability of $750$ with same volume maintaining same current of $0 . 75A$ in the solenoid, the fractional change in the magnetic moment of the core would be approximately $\left(\dfrac{x}{499}\right) .$ Find the value of $x .$
questions.solution:
$\overset{\to}{M} = \dfrac{magnetic moment \left(\overset{\to}{m}\right)}{V}$
$⇒ χ\overset{\to}{H} = \overset{\to}{m}V$
$⇒ \overset{\to}{m} = \left({\mu}_{r} - 1\right)NiV$
$∴ \dfrac{\Deltam}{m} = \dfrac{[ \left(750 - 1\right) - \left(500 - 1\right) ] NiV}{\left(500 - 1\right)NiV} = 250$

questions.q: The current required to be passed through a solenoid of $15cm$ length and $60$ turns in order to demagnetise a bar magnet of magnetic intensity $2 . 4 \times {10}^{3}A{m}^{– 1}$ is ________ $A$.
questions.solution:
The magnetic intensity is

$H = \dfrac{B}{{\mu}_{0}} - M$

For $M = 0$, it can be written

$H = \left(\dfrac{B}{{\mu}_{0}}\right) = ni$

The data given is

$H = 2 . 4 \times {10}^{3}A{m}^{- 1}l = 15 \times {10}^{- 2}mN = 60$

Using the relation, $n = \dfrac{N}{l}$ and $H = ni$, the value of the current is,

$i = \dfrac{H}{n} = \dfrac{2 . 4 \times {10}^{3} \times 15 \times {10}^{- 2}}{60} = 6A$

questions.q: A deuteron and a proton moving with equal kinetic energy enter into to a uniform magnetic field at right angle to the field. If ${r}_{d}$ and ${r}_{p}$ are the radii of their circular paths respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{{r}_{d}}{{r}_{p}}$ will be $\sqrt{x}: 1$ where $x$ is _____ .
questions.solution:
As we know, radius of circular path followed by charged particle under perpendicular magnetic field is given by,

$R = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$ and $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Therefore,

$⇒ R = \dfrac{\sqrt{2m\left(KE\right)}}{qB}$ Then, $R ∝ \dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{q}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{R}_{d}}{{R}_{p}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{d}}{{m}_{p}}} \times \dfrac{{q}_{p}}{{q}_{d}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{1}} \times \dfrac{1}{1} = \sqrt{2}: 1$

Thus, $x = 2$.
